questions.stem: In spinal anaesthesia, where is the local anaesthetic injected?
options: Into the epidural space outside the dura
Into the subcutaneous tissue over the lumbar spine
Into the cerebrospinal fluid in the spinal canal
Around a spinal nerve root in the foramen

questions.stem: How does local anaesthetic in spinal anaesthesia produce its effect?
questions.answer: Disrupts nerve conduction in the spinal nerve roots and spinal cord

questions.stem: Spinal anaesthesia is mainly used for surgery ____ the umbilicus.
Which sensory level does spinal anaesthesia need for gynaecology procedures such as D&C and hysteroscopy?
What sensory level does spinal anaesthesia need for urology surgery?
What sensory level does spinal anaesthesia need for procedures involving the ureters?
Which lower limb orthopaedic procedure is a recognised use of spinal anaesthesia?
Compared with general anaesthesia, what is the analgesia difference 6h after spinal anaesthesia?
Which airway-related risks of general anaesthesia does spinal anaesthesia avoid?
questions.answer: Airway instrumentation and its risks, including aspiration

questions.stem: Compared with general anaesthesia, which postoperative complication does spinal anaesthesia reduce?
Spinal anaesthesia usually gives no ____ benefit over general anaesthesia, except in hip fracture.
What fetal advantage does spinal anaesthesia offer for caesarean section?
questions.answer: Minimal drug transfer to the fetus

questions.stem: What may spinal anaesthesia failure require?
What is the key limitation on the duration of a single spinal anaesthetic?
questions.answer: Fixed and limited; cannot be extended

questions.stem: Spinal anaesthesia needs lateral or sitting positioning. Which surgical setup can rule this out?
When under spinal anaesthesia, why might a patient move during surgery?
Which two haemodynamic changes from rapid sympathectomy cause sudden hypotension in spinal anaesthesia?
questions.answer: Fall in SVR and fall in preload

questions.stem: What does PDPH stand for as a complication of spinal anaesthesia?
Spinal anaesthesia blocks which two broad groups of nerve fibres?
questions.answer: Sympathetic and somatic (sensory and motor) fibres

questions.stem: How quickly does spinal anaesthesia usually take effect?
How far does the sympathetic block of spinal anaesthesia extend beyond the motor block?
How far does the pain and touch block of spinal anaesthesia extend beyond the motor block?
Does spinal anaesthesia cause cognitive effects, and if so, when?
questions.answer: No, unless hypotension reduces cerebral blood flow

Which levels carry the cardiac accelerator sympathetic fibres blocked by a high spinal?
Which reflex can make heart rate fall, rather than rise, after spinal anaesthesia?
What is the usual respiratory effect of spinal anaesthesia?
How do hepatic and renal blood flow change as mean arterial pressure falls during spinal anaesthesia?
Spinal anaesthesia can block sacral parasympathetic outflow to the bladder, causing urinary ____.
In spinal anaesthesia from T6 to L1, what happens to gut peristalsis?
What endocrine effect does spinal anaesthesia have?
At what platelet count is spinal anaesthesia definitely avoided?
